summary: The operator asked how an organization's signing key works under quorum control, and after the answer asked to write it into the spec, slot it in the sequence, push to main, and continue autonomously. MYCELIUM_NETWORK_SPEC.md section 6 gained the organization-key governance model: the design is a split, because an org key does two jobs. Everyday issuance — signing memberships — stays fast: a clerk signs and it is valid instantly, and other officials co-sign later as ratification that only accumulates (no redo, no revoke), which needs no new cryptography because the tapit-attest envelope is multi-signature by nature. Constitutional acts — changing officials, rotating the key, joining a larger org, dissolving — require a true M-of-N threshold, the HEARTWOOD higher-threshold-for-higher-stakes principle. In the full quorum model the org's authority is distributed across the officials' wallets — there is no single org key to steal. This was slotted into the phasing as Phase 5f, and PLAN.md updated to 5a-5f. A Phase 5c (Nostr transport) design sketch was written so the next Layer 3 increment is ready to bless. Branch and main both pushed.

why.text: Operator: 'Yes, and put it where it goes in the sequence ... push to main ... you continue on.' The governance answer was grounded in the existing doctrine (spec section 6's deferral, HEARTWOOD's threshold-by-stakes, tapit-attest's native multi-signature). With the operator stepping away, autonomous work was kept to the well-determined and safe: the approved spec enrichment and a design sketch for the forky Phase 5c — not a solo cut of a big networking feature.
